generated.title: San Francisco 1906: One Minute of Shaking, Three Days of Fire #shorts
generated.description:
On April 18, 1906, a magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck San Francisco.

The San Andreas Fault ruptured across nearly 300 miles. Water mains broke, fires spread for three days, and approximately 28,000 buildings were destroyed.

More than half the city's population was left homeless. Thousands lost their lives.

This cinematic reconstruction combines authentic photographs from the U.S. National Archives with AI-generated historical illustrations. AI-generated scenes are not authentic footage from 1906.

Sources:
- USGS: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/events/1906calif/18april/
- USGS casualties and damage: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/events/1906calif/18april/casualties.php
- National Park Service: https://home.nps.gov/prsf/historyculture/1906-earthquake-fire-fighting.htm
- U.S. National Archives: Record Group 92 photographs (listed in the credits below)
